stem:
Meena has two bar magnets in her science kit at home. Her teacher in school has asked her to store them carefully so that they do not lose their magnetism.
Which way of storing the two bar magnets is correct?

options.text: Keep the magnets with like poles on the same side, a piece of wood between them, and soft iron pieces across the ends
Keep the magnets with unlike poles on the same side, a piece of wood between them, and soft iron pieces across the ends
Keep the magnets touching each other directly, with soft iron pieces across the ends and no wood between them
Keep the magnets near the mobile phone charger, with soft rubber pieces across the ends

teacher.key_rationale: Bar magnets are stored in pairs with unlike poles on the same side, a piece of wood between them, and soft iron keepers across the ends; this preserves magnetism. A has like poles together (wrong pole arrangement), C omits the wood separator and lets magnets touch, D places magnets near a device and uses rubber instead of soft iron keepers.
